metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: data available from the corresponding author upon request
metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, China, including video frames for vehicle location extraction and 10-minute traffic volumes used for simulation calibration.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper states that the data used to support the results are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle coordinates (xi, yi) from raw video frames to create position matrices mt where vehicles are represented by constant UV.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic tools not named, basic parameters provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Stacks N consecutive position matrices after down-sampling to represent the traffic state st, including signal state information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, dimensions specified, but generic tools not linked to libraries.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a dual-output CNN using multitask learning to estimate Q-values and predict speed/queue length. Uses experience replay and a target network for stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, almost all parameters and tools specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained policy in a SUMO simulation of a real-world freeway segment (Qingdao-Huangdao tunnel) over 20 experiments.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, hardware and simulation parameters well-defined.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Removes information from specific subareas of the control area to test the impact on travel time performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, subarea division logic described but exact masking method is brief.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training parameters and simulator (SUMO) are specified, but the exact real-world dataset used for calibration is not publicly linked.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of vehicle travel times in the mainline for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methodology and comparison baselines are well-defined; results follow logically from the described simulation setup.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2: Mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean travel times (seconds) for 20 experiments across three control scenarios, including percentage improvements.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed per-experiment results provided; reproducibility limited primarily by the availability of the specific input traffic volume data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed distribution across distance and time for the three evaluated control strategies.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visual representation of simulation outcomes; consistent with other reported metrics but depends on unreleased raw traffic data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11: Queue length at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plot of queue lengths at the on-ramp for the three scenarios, including variance/confidence intervals.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison of a key performance indicator; procedure for measurement in SUMO is standard.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream traffic volume over time for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Aggregated simulation data; specific aggregation intervals are clear from the x-axis.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16: Travel time with perturbed input data.
nodes_sink.description: Box plot showing the impact on travel time when information from different subareas (1-8) is removed.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The perturbation method (removing subarea data) is clearly described and the results directly support the claim of spatial sensitivity.
